clue.text: No mean economic policy

parts.note: a policy that never settles at a steady average but lurches between braking and accelerating the economy, halt then advance

explanation.definitionFit: Stop-go was the British name for alternating restraint and expansion of the economy, never a middle course.

clue.text: One feels for the octopus

parts.note: not someone sympathising with the creature but an arm the creature uses to touch and grope

explanation.definitionFit: An octopus's arms are feelers it uses to explore and grasp by touch.

clue.text: Go-getter's hairstyle? Now, it's all off

definitions.meaning: a whimsical haircut for a dynamic, ambitious person
a moment when the electricity supply fails

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a failure of the electricity supply, and jokingly a haircut suited to someone with drive.

clue.text: Does he not get even casual work?

definitions.text: Does he not get even casual work?

parts.words: Does he not get even casual work?
parts.note: reads as a pitying question about an unemployed man, but asks whether his work is the opposite of even, that is irregular

explanation.definitionFit: A handyman does assorted casual tasks, the odd jobs, rather than regular employment.

clue.text: Scottish PM wielded the knife

definitions.note: a description of the man rather than a noun: the one who wielded the knife

parts.note: Mac is a common prefix of Scottish surnames, and a word for a Scot
Edward Heath was British Prime Minister 1970-74

explanation.surface: A Scottish prime minister did the stabbing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the character: Macheath is the highwayman of The Beggar's Opera and The Threepenny Opera, sung of as Mack the Knife.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Macheath is the villain celebrated in the song Mack the Knife, so he is the one who carried the blade.

clue.text: Indemnify states for damaging USA's future

indicators.note: damaged material is broken apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Paying compensation to states for harm done would ruin America's prospects.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest destiny was the 19th-century belief that the United States was destined to expand across the continent.

clue.text: Sharp instrument drives cattle round a pound

indicators.note: the cattle word goes around the other letters

parts.note: to herd is to drive livestock along
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A drover uses a pointed stick to move his herd into a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' looks like an animal enclosure, fitting the cattle, but is the unit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A halberd is a long-handled weapon with an axe blade and spike.

clue.text: Pretty artistic boys, mostly Greek, including Thomas

indicators.note: the shortened Greek word holds the other name inside it
most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: Attic means of Athens, so Greek
Sir Thomas More, the Tudor statesman

explanation.surface: Attractive young men in an artistic circle, most of them Greek, include one called Thomas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thomas' tempts as TOM; it is the Tudor statesman. 'mostly' trims ATTIC to ATTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoretti are little cupids, the chubby winged boys of Renaissance art.

clue.text: They don't think hoods regularly take in The Bill

indicators.note: the picked letters enclose the rest, as a building takes in guests
every other letter of the word is taken

parts.note: an ad, an advertisement, is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: Thoughtless thugs routinely take in the police, the Old Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Bill' suggests the Old Bill, British slang for the police; here it is THE plus an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotheads act rashly without stopping to think.

clue.text: Unable to leave the White House?

definitions.text: Unable to leave the White House?

parts.words: Unable to leave the White House?
parts.note: not the US president's residence but any house turned white by heavy drifts, trapping those inside

explanation.definitionFit: People trapped at home by a heavy fall of snow cannot get out, so their house is white.

clue.text: Call for the strike, but so unable to bat on

definitions.meaning: a union cry summoning every member to stop work
in cricket, a side with ten batsmen dismissed has no one left to bat

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a shout calling every worker to strike and the cricket term for an innings ended with all wickets down.

clue.text: Withdraw over a river and win

indicators.note: the withdrawing phrase is laid over the other letters, covering them on both sides

parts.note: to cry off is to back out of an arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone retreats across a river and still comes out the victor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts A and R inside CRY OFF, splitting it after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry off a prize is to win it.

clue.text: Difficult part, the lead in Electra

parts.note: to part is to divide or cut off, as to sever

indicators.note: the leading letter of the following word is the one taken

explanation.surface: An actress finds the title role in the Greek tragedy Electra a hard part to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' looks like a noun for an acting role but is the verb to divide.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe test is a hard or demanding one, so severe can mean difficult.

clue.text: Revealed Mark gatecrashed?

annotationWithheld.why: Revealed Mark gatecrashed? (8): the parse is M inside UNASKED, with 'gatecrashed' both giving UNASKED and signalling the insertion, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Seize my hand over reference work that's not to be used

indicators.note: to hand over is to turn over, so the preceding pair of words is read backwards

parts.note: to grab is to seize
my as the object form is me, so the possessive stands in for the pronoun
the OED, the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a dictionary from another person, though it is off limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seize my hand' reads as grabbing someone's hand; in fact 'hand over' reverses the GRAB ME pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something embargoed is banned from release or use, as a press statement is until a set time.

clue.text: Go all weak — I'm an officer

parts.note: the speaker referring to themself, read as the word me
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: Someone swoons at the sight of a person in uniform introducing themself as an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To melt is to soften with tenderness, to go weak at the knees.

clue.text: Speaker understands my French in town

indicators.note: read as under-stands: the speaker word stands beneath the French word in this down entry

parts.note: mon is French for my
a mouth is what speaks; also slang for a talker

explanation.surface: A speaker understands enough French to get by in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'understands' looks like comprehension but splits as 'under stands'. Monmouth is a town in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Monmouth is a market town in south-east Wales.

clue.text: More imperious order I'll get redrafted

indicators.note: a redrafted text is rewritten, so these letters are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A haughty boss sends back an order to be rewritten.
explanation.definitionFit: Lordly means haughty and imperious, and this is its comparative form.

clue.text: Salute king — one's succeeded

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
one is I in Roman numerals, so one's is I'S
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A courtier greets the monarch on news that someone has come to the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss on the cheek or hand is a form of greeting or salute.

clue.text: Producer of Bourbon range fortunate to get new head

parts.note: ken is range of knowledge, as in beyond my ken

indicators.note: the first letter of the fortunate word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: lucky means fortunate

explanation.surface: A distillery is fortunate to appoint a new boss for its bourbon range.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which new head LUCKY gets; the answer settles it as T. 'Bourbon' suggests the French royal house but is the whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: Bourbon whiskey is made chiefly in the American state of Kentucky, named after Bourbon County.

clue.text: Need ears tuned to this?

indicators.note: tuned notes are adjusted into harmony, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A listener needs a good ear to appreciate this music.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, the clue asks what you should have your ears tuned to: a love song sung beneath a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a song performed for a lover, meant to be listened to.

clue.text: I bleed in being operated on, needing to be taken off table?

definitions.text: needing to be taken off table?
definitions.note: an adjective phrase: food unfit to eat is removed from the dining table

indicators.note: the letters undergo an operation, as in surgery, and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient haemorrhaging during surgery must be lifted off the operating table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'table' suggests the operating table, but the definition means the dining table: food you cannot eat gets cleared away.
explanation.definitionFit: Inedible food is unfit to eat, so it is cleared from the dining table.

clue.text: Most of pub almost sober, for a change

indicators.note: the pub word loses its final letter

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: the sober word is left a letter short at its end

parts.note: steady means sober and level-headed

explanation.surface: A drinker in the pub, nearly sober, decides on a change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' cuts INN to IN; 'almost' cuts STEADY to STEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead means as an alternative, in place of something else, which is what doing something for a change implies.

clue.text: Country by the sea —- all her visitors got stoned

definitions.note: a description of a woman whose callers were turned to rock

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
the USA is a country

explanation.surface: A coastal resort where every visitor ends up drunk or high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stoned' suggests drugs; in fact the Gorgon of Greek myth turned all who looked at her to stone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Gorgon's gaze petrified every onlooker, so her visitors were literally turned to stone.

clue.text: Salesmen back to swallow luxury drink

indicators.note: the first piece takes the second into its middle, as a mouth takes in food
the salesmen word is written backwards

parts.note: reps are sales representatives
the Ritz is a byword for luxury, from the London hotel

explanation.surface: Sales staff return to down an expensive cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REPS into SPER before the luxury hotel goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritzer is a mixed drink of white wine and soda water.

clue.text: Various football teams in league

definitions.meaning: many clubs carry the word in their name, such as Manchester and Leeds

explanation.definitionFit: The word ends many club names like Leeds and Newcastle, and also means joined in alliance.

clue.text: Two clubs boy joined to be well-protected

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A youngster joins two clubs and finds himself well looked after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two clubs' gives two different clubs: a golf iron and the bridge abbreviation C.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironclad literally means armoured with iron plates, hence strongly protected.

clue.text: How a seventh son acquired extraordinary third eye?

definitions.note: names the means of acquiring rather than the gift: by inheritance

indicators.note: something out of the ordinary has been reordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seventh son came by his uncanny psychic sight, the third eye.
explanation.walkthrough: Folklore gives the seventh son of a seventh son second sight, passed down by birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Traits passed from parents to offspring come by heredity, the way a seventh son inherits his gift in folklore.

clue.text: By coming in late, rejected flat out here perhaps

indicators.note: rejected things are thrown back, so the assembled letters are read in reverse
the first word enters the second piece

parts.note: the late person is one who is dead

explanation.surface: Someone arriving late is turned away and goes to lie down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' gives DEBYAD before 'rejected' turns it round; 'late' means deceased, not tardy.
explanation.definitionFit: A daybed is a couch for resting in the daytime, where one might lie flat out.
